about: Human-labelled answers for calibrating the grounding judge. 'good' means every claim in the answer is supported by the passages. 'bad' means at least one claim is wrong, contradicted, or not in the passages. Passages are excerpts from lambda/data/documents. Run: python pipeline/judge_calibrate.py

examples.label: good
examples.question: How many paid sick days do I get per year?

passages.title: Sick Leave and Absence Policy
passages.content:
- United States: 10 paid sick days per calendar year, non-accruing, resetting on 1 January
- United Kingdom: company sick pay at full salary for up to 8 weeks in any 12-month period, then Statutory Sick Pay
- Germany: continued payment of salary (Entgeltfortzahlung) for up to 6 weeks, then Krankengeld from the health insurer
- India: 12 days paid sick leave per calendar year

examples.answer:
In the United States you get 10 paid sick days per calendar year. They do not accrue and reset on 1 January.

Sources: Sick Leave and Absence Policy

examples.answer:
In the UK you receive company sick pay at full salary for up to 8 weeks in any 12-month period. After that, Statutory Sick Pay applies.

Sources: Sick Leave and Absence Policy

examples.label: good
examples.question: When do I need a doctor's note?

passages.title: Sick Leave and Absence Policy
passages.content:
A certificate is required from the fourth consecutive working day of absence in the United States, the United Kingdom and India. In Germany a certificate is required from the fourth calendar day, and your manager may request one from the first day.
Send certificates to hr-help@northwind.example, not to your manager.

examples.answer:
In the US, UK and India you need a medical certificate from the fourth consecutive working day of absence. In Germany it is from the fourth calendar day, and your manager may ask for one from the first day. Send it to hr-help@northwind.example, not to your manager.

Sources: Sick Leave and Absence Policy

examples.label: good
examples.question: How many days of bereavement leave do I get if a parent dies?

passages.title: Bereavement Leave
passages.content:
- 10 working days on the death of a partner, child, or pregnancy loss at any stage
- 5 working days on the death of a parent, sibling, grandparent or grandchild
- 3 working days on the death of another close family member or a close friend
- 1 working day to attend a funeral in any other case
These are minimums. If you need more time, ask.

examples.answer:
You get 5 working days of paid bereavement leave on the death of a parent. That is a minimum: if you need more time, ask.

Sources: Bereavement Leave

passages.title: Bereavement Leave

examples.answer:
No. You do not need to provide any documentation. On the death of a partner you get 10 working days of paid bereavement leave, and it does not come out of your paid time off.

Sources: Bereavement Leave

examples.question: When do I need a receipt, and how long do I have to claim?

passages.title: Expense and Reimbursement Policy
passages.content:
Claims go through Expensify, linked from Workday. Attach a receipt for anything over 25 US dollars. Below that, a line in the description is enough.
Submit within 60 days of the spend. Claims older than 60 days need your manager and Finance to approve, and claims older than 6 months are not paid at all.

examples.answer:

passages.title: Employee Assistance Programme
passages.content: Counselling is available by phone, video or in person, usually within five working days and sooner in an emergency. The standard allocation is eight sessions per issue per year, and the provider will say if more are needed and arrange them.

examples.answer:
Eight sessions per issue per year as standard. If more are needed, the provider will say so and arrange them.

Sources: Employee Assistance Programme

examples.label: good
examples.question: Will my manager find out if I call the EAP?

passages.title: Employee Assistance Programme
passages.content:
Northwind receives a quarterly report showing how many people used the service and the broad categories of issue, with no names and no details.
Your manager will never be told that you called, what you discussed, or that you are receiving counselling.

examples.answer:
No. Your manager will never be told that you called, what you discussed, or that you are receiving counselling. Northwind only sees a quarterly report with no names or details.

Sources: Employee Assistance Programme
